result.title: Less is More: Concise Retrieval and Critic-based Re-ranking for Composed Image Retrieval
result.summary: Zero-shot composed image retrieval (ZS-CIR) aims to retrieve a target image based on a reference image and modification text. Recent approaches commonly rely on large vision-language models to generate target image captions for retrieval. However, these captions may include redundant semantic details, introducing noise when retrieving the target image and leading to suboptimal retrieval results. To address this issue, we propose Less-is-More CIR, a two-stage training-free framework that combines Concise Retrieval and Critic Re-ranking. In the first stage, concise target-oriented captions are generated that preserve only the most discriminative modification semantics, thereby reducing semantic noise in the retrieval. In the second stage, a critic re-rank module further evaluates the retrieved candidates from the perspectives of modification consistency and reference preservation. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework for the ZS-CIR. Our code is available at: https://github.com/dxlabskku/LM-CIR.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文面向零样本组合图像检索，提出两阶段免训练框架：先由大视觉语言模型生成只保留判别性修改语义的简洁目标描述以减少语义噪声，再用 critic 模块从修改一致性与参考图像保持两方面对候选做重排。
AI.relevance_reason: 检索任务本身偏离 LVR 主线，但其「精简内容以抑制冗余语义」与免训练 critic 重排属可核查的筛选与验证线索，可能启发 latent 假设或视觉证据的择优与打分，需看 critic 的具体判据设计。
